title: Sample holder development for in-situ EBAC mapping of thin-film conductivity
author: Løge, Kristiansen, et al.
materials: For our case study, TiO2 films were prepared on a custom sample holder (described below) that provides two separated electrode contacts. We used TiO2 nanoparticulate powder (P25) purchased from Sigma Aldrich dispersed in isopropanol (IPA) to form a casting solution. Achieving a uniform, well-connected film required optimizing the TiO2:IPA ratio and dispersion technique. In preliminary tests, a 1:1 (wt:wt) TiO2–IPA mixture produced thick deposits that cracked upon drying, resulting in isolated domains with poor connectivity (Fig. 1a). Diluting the suspension (approximately 1:10 by weight) yielded a continuous granular film with no cracks (Fig. 1b). Ultrasonication of the TiO2 suspension for ∼10 min prior to deposition was employed to break up agglomerates and improve particle dispersion (Fig. 1c). Ultrasonication was performed in a heated water bath at 65°C, using the model Ironeside 506,482.Fig. 1SEM images of drop-casted thin films of TiO2 with different mixing ratios and dispersion methods. (a) a 1:1 (wt:wt) TiO2–IPA mixture with no ultrasonication. (b) a 1:10 (wt:wt) TiO2–IPA mixture with no ultrasonication. (c) a 1:10 (wt:wt) TiO2–IPA mixture with 10 min of ultrasonication.Fig 1: dummy alt text

Each film was deposited through drop-casting ∼1–2 µL of the TiO2/IPA mixture into a channel on the sample holder (spanning the gap between electrodes) with a pipette. Drop-casting was performed in multiple small installments using a gentle rocking motion to spread the solution evenly. Films were air-dried for approximately 1 h at room temperature to evaporate the solvent, and this process was repeated 1–2 times to build up a thicker layer in a controlled manner. All samples were prepared and measured on the same day to avoid sedimentation or particle re-agglomeration. We found that these practices (using a high dilution ratio, sonication, and layered deposition) consistently produced TiO2 films that visually covered the electrode gap with minimal cracking.

The deposited TiO2 layers should therefore be regarded as irregular drop-cast particulate films with no precise control of film thickness beyond drop volume and total number of drops deposited. Film thickness was not independently measured by profilometry, AFM, or cross-sectional imaging in the present study, which limits any transport analysis based on absolute thickness. However, if the proposed methodology was combined with a profilometry measurement, it would further strengthen the possible analysis.

steps.title: Prepare TiO₂ suspension
steps.instruction: Mix TiO₂ P25 powder (Sigma Aldrich) with isopropanol at a 1:10 weight‑to‑weight ratio, then ultrasonicate the suspension for approximately 10 minutes in a heated water bath at 65 °C using the Ironeside 506,482 model.

substeps.instruction: Weigh TiO₂ and IPA to achieve a 1:10 (wt:wt) ratio.
Combine the powders and solvent in a suitable vessel.
Place the vessel in the Ironeside 506,482 water bath set to 65 °C.
Ultrasonicate for ~10 min to break up agglomerates.

steps.title: Deposit TiO₂ film by drop‑casting
steps.instruction: Using a pipette, drop‑cast 1–2 µL of the TiO₂/IPA mixture into the channel on the custom sample holder that spans the electrode gap, gently rock the holder to spread the liquid, air‑dry for about 1 hour at room temperature, and repeat the deposition 1–2 times to build a thicker layer; prepare and measure all samples on the same day.

substeps.instruction: Load 1–2 µL of suspension into a pipette.
Deposit the drop into the channel between the electrodes.
Apply a gentle rocking motion to spread the solution evenly.
Allow the film to air‑dry for ~1 h at room temperature.
Repeat the drop‑casting and drying 1–2 additional times as needed.
Ensure all samples are prepared and measured on the same day.

steps.title: Configure SEM for EBAC measurement
steps.instruction: Install the JEOL JSM‑7200F scanning electron microscope equipped with the Point Electronic EBIC module, set the instrument to high‑vacuum mode, choose an acceleration voltage between 5 and 15 keV (optionally test <5 keV), and set the beam current to 2–18 nA.

substeps.instruction: Mount the sample holder in the JEOL JSM‑7200F.
Activate high‑vacuum mode.
Select an acceleration voltage of 5–15 keV (or <5 keV for penetration depth tests).
Adjust the beam current to fall within 2–18 nA.

steps.title: Acquire secondary‑electron images
steps.instruction: Capture secondary electron (SE) images of the TiO₂ film and electrode region to verify that the film bridges the gap and to identify any cracks or uncovered areas.

steps.title: Perform line scans across gap
steps.instruction: Program the electron beam to scan a linear path perpendicular to the electrode gap, crossing from one electrode through the film to the opposite electrode, record the induced current, repeat the scans at different applied biases, keep the scan speed moderate, and acquire at least three line scans per bias for reliable averaging.

substeps.instruction: Define a line scan trajectory across the gap.
Set the desired applied bias for the scan.
Adjust scan speed to allow sufficient current averaging.
Execute a minimum of three scans for each bias.
Repeat the procedure for additional bias values.

steps.title: Optional 2D raster mapping
steps.instruction: If desired, perform a raster (2D) scan covering the electrode gap and adjacent electrode areas, collecting the induced current at each pixel to generate a conductivity map.

steps.title: Limit beam exposure and monitor film
steps.instruction: Avoid high electron doses that could damage the TiO₂ film—especially limit repeated scans at voltages >10 keV—periodically re‑image the area with SE to check for visible changes, and record all line‑profile and image data using the Point Electronic DISS5 software.

substeps.instruction: Restrict the number of high‑voltage (>10 keV) scans.
After each set of scans, capture a fresh SE image to inspect the film.
Save all acquired data with the Point Electronic DISS5 system.

description: To show that the workflow can distinguish an electrically open gap from a bridged thin film and produce a response with spatial information, we include two representative datasets: (1) EBAC maps acquired at three applied biases (0 V, 4 V, 9 V), and (2) line scans performed on the same holder geometry with and without a TiO2 film spanning the electrode gap.
